Na__AppData__AppConfig__.description: Runtime configuration for Noble BIM Asset Tools. Loaded once at boot by Na__AppCore__ConfigLoader__.js and exposed read-only through Na__AppCore__AppState__.js.

tolerances.description: All linear tolerances are in millimetres, the internal working unit.
tolerances.weldVertexToleranceNote: Vertices closer than this are treated as coincident when checking for open edges. One micron - tight enough not to weld real detail, loose enough to absorb float32 noise.
tolerances.degenerateTriangleNote: Triangles with an area below this in square millimetres are reported as degenerate slivers.
tolerances.originDistanceWarningNote: 100 metres. Geometry sitting further than this from the world origin loses float32 precision and is flagged. Common with georeferenced UK Revit exports carrying Ordnance Survey National Grid coordinates.
tolerances.originDistanceCriticalNote: 1 kilometre. Past this, single-precision rounding is visible at millimetre scale and re-centring is strongly advised before export.
tolerances.exportVerifyToleranceNote: Maximum permitted bounding-box drift in millimetres between the source model and the re-read exported GLB. Anything larger fails the export verification.

occtTessellation.description: Controls how OpenCascade converts true BREP surfaces into triangles. Lower deflection means more triangles and a closer fit to the real surface.
occtTessellation.linearDeflectionNote: Maximum chordal deviation in millimetres between the tessellated facet and the true surface. 0.1 mm is well inside architectural tolerance.
occtTessellation.angularDeflectionNote: Maximum angular deviation in radians across a curved span.

viewer.cameraFovNote: A narrow 35 degree field of view keeps orthographic-like proportions, which reads better for component inspection than a wide lens.

materials.backFaceColourNote: Reversed faces render in this red so inverted normals are obvious on sight, which matters because SketchUp imports them reversed too.

glbExport.bakeScaleNote: The unit conversion is baked into vertex positions rather than left on a node transform. Some importers silently drop node scale, and a dropped scale is a 1000x error that is easy to miss on an isolated component.
glbExport.upAxisNote: glTF fixes +Y as up. Source BIM content is Z-up, so a single -90 degree rotation about X is applied at export and recorded in the report.
glbExport.useDracoNote: Deliberately off. Draco is lossy for vertex positions at default quantisation and this tool exists to preserve dimensional accuracy.

ingest.maxFileSizeNote: Guard against a browser tab running out of memory. IFC parsing peaks at roughly four times the file size in RAM.
